paths.description: Homepage URL as served from this audit location: static EEA/UK regional restriction notice. Represents the only reachable www.yahoo.co.jp template. Covered desktop, mobile, dark/reduced-motion/contrast preferences, keyboard focus, raw HTML/no-JS, performance, network, security, accessibility, and memory. Not covered: Japan-only portal, search/news/content/account/commerce templates, because the edge consistently returns the same intentional 403 notice for this region.

findings.summary: The notice is hard-coded to a light theme and does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the computed root background remained rgb(255,255,255), color-scheme remained normal, and the dark screenshot was pixel-equivalent in appearance to the light capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, and link colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The page does not adapt its controls or colors when the user requests more contrast.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more probe matched the preference but returned the same #1a75ff/#1f78ff link colors; axe measured ratios of 4.17:1 and 4.04:1, below WCAG AA for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-contrast: more treatment with stronger link contrast and preserve visible focus and control boundaries in forced-colors mode.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint was slightly outside the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: The CDP trace measured FCP and LCP at 2768 ms. It found zero long tasks and zero TBT, indicating the delay is network/render-path rather than JavaScript execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical render path by consolidating or inlining critical CSS and preloading only the key font/image resources needed for the first viewport.

findings.summary: Primary and inline link colors do not meet WCAG AA contrast against white.
findings.evidence: axe reported serious color-contrast violations across Japanese and English links: #1a75ff at 4.17:1 and #1f78ff at 4.04:1 versus the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker blue that reaches at least 4.5:1 on white and retain a non-color link cue such as underline, especially in prose.

findings.summary: The document has no H1, starts with H3 then H2, and nests the contentinfo footer inside main.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found headings H3,H2,H2 and no H1; axe reported page-has-heading-one and landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level violations. Keyboard focus itself remained visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one H1 for the access notice, place section headings beneath it in order, and move the footer outside the main landmark.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration disables pinch zoom.
findings.evidence: The live meta viewport is width=device-width,user-scalable=no; axe classified this as a critical meta-viewport violation. Narrow viewport reflow itself had zero horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and do not set maximum-scale below 5 so users can magnify content.

findings.summary: The logo lacks an explicit height and is delivered vastly larger than its rendered size.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found a 1933 px-wide PNG displayed at 170 px, with width but no height attribute and no srcset. Observed CLS was zero in this run, but the intrinsic-size and delivery hygiene remain weak.
findings.suggestedFix: Export an appropriately sized modern-format logo, provide width and height attributes, and add responsive sources only if multiple display sizes are required.

findings.summary: The notice has a descriptive title but no meta description.
findings.evidence: The rendered and raw HTML both preserve the title, while DOM and discoverability probes found no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise bilingual meta description explaining the regional availability notice and available alternatives.

findings.summary: The 403 notice response omits several baseline browser security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, but found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a restrictive CSP, long-lived HSTS after subdomain review, nosniff, a deliberate Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy on the notice response.

findings.summary: Defense-in-depth policies are incomplete despite clickjacking protection being present.
findings.evidence: X-Frame-Options protects against framing, but the response has no frame-ancestors CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP-based XSS defense.
findings.suggestedFix: Define defense-in-depth headers consistently at the edge for all status responses, including regional 403 pages.

findings.summary: The bilingual Japanese/English document has no document language declaration.
findings.evidence: The DOM returned an empty html.lang and axe reported a serious html-has-lang violation. The page contains both Japanese and English sections but does not mark the English section with lang="en".
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang="ja" and mark the English article or its container with lang="en"; use logical properties for translation-safe layout.

findings.summary: The only content image is oversized and uses a legacy PNG without responsive selection.
findings.evidence: The image is naturally 1933 px wide but displayed at 170 px, has no srcset, and transfers 13 KB as PNG; the entire page transfers 73.8 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an appropriately dimensioned WebP/AVIF or optimized PNG at the actual display density and declare intrinsic dimensions.

taskList.title: Restore zoom and correct document language/heading landmarks
Add complete browser security headers to the regional 403 response
Raise link contrast and adapt colors for dark/high-contrast preferences
Reduce the render path and optimize the oversized logo
Add a useful bilingual meta description
